title: Sea Scout
paragraphOne: Being a sea scout essentially means the same thing as being a regular scout: learning by doing, cooperating, and showing consideration, but the water is our main classroom.
heading: The Water as the Focus
paragraphTwo: The biggest difference is that activities during the warm half of the year almost exclusively take place on the sea.
listItemOne: Sailing: You learn to handle different types of boats, from small dinghies to larger keelboats. You practice tacking, running with the wind, and handling different wind conditions.
listItemTwo: Seamanship: This includes everything from knots and splicing to being able to navigate using nautical charts, a compass, and understanding weather reports.
listItemThree: Safety: Water safety is essential. You learn to swim in clothes, use life jackets, what to do if someone falls overboard, and general 'good seamanship'.
